reason: The winding drum and its bearing bracket look like the first part of the lifting mechanism to mount on the crane.
expectation: The drum and bracket will be fitted to the crane frame.

alternatives.reason: The crank may need to be assembled with the drum before it is mounted.

effect: The drum had to be assembled with the crank first; the resulting hand winch may now fit the crane.
reaction: The automatic assembly made the failed guess useful, and the explanation of the longer crank was interesting.
reason: The assembled winch should mount on the crane to wind the lifting cord.
expectation: The hand winch will be fitted to the crane.

effect: The winch is mounted, so the crane can now be fitted with its lifting cord.
reason: The cord and hook should connect the winch to the load through the tip pulley.
expectation: The cord will be routed over the pulley and attached to the winch.

effect: The lifting line is installed, leaving the holding and stability parts to fit before the basket lift.
reason: The pawl should engage the winch's ratchet to hold a raised load.
expectation: The pawl and release lever will be fitted to the crane's winch.

alternatives.reason: The ballast also looks useful for stabilizing the crane before lifting.

effect: The pawl can hold the rope but cannot prevent tipping, so the crane's stability still needs attention.
reaction: The distinction between holding the load and stabilizing the crane is useful.
reason: The rear ballast should help counter the load before testing the crane.
expectation: The ballast will be fitted to the rear of the crane to improve its stability.

alternatives.reason: The test weight could reveal how the crane behaves before lifting the basket.

effect: The ballast and pawl are fitted, and the crane is ready for a low test of both.
reaction: Testing the two safeguards together makes sense.
reason: The padded test weight is intended for the low test before lifting the basket.

choice.with: Ballasted holding crane ready for a test

expectation: The crane will lift the test weight low and check its stability and holding pawl.

effect: The low test confirmed that the ballast keeps the feet down and the pawl holds the drum; the basket is the next load to try.
reaction: The explanation of holding the crank while releasing the pawl makes the lowering mechanism clearer.
reason: The tested crane is ready to lift, hold and lower the cargo basket.
expectation: The crane will lift the basket, hold it with the pawl and lower it gently.

effect: The basket lift confirmed that the assembled crane can hold a load and lower it under control, completing the goal.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the separate stability and holding mechanisms work together in a delivery.

mostWorthwhile.text: The low test was most worthwhile: it showed how the ballast and pawl do different jobs, and how to lower a load safely.

leastWorthwhile.text: Mounting the winch and adding the cord were straightforward assembly steps, with less to discover than the test.

surprise.text: I appreciated the distinction that the pawl can prevent the drum from unwinding but cannot stop the whole crane tipping.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary. My first mounting guess was wrong, but the compatibility feedback made the required assembly clear.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see what the fair does with these constructions; the crane's practical mechanisms made this chapter worth the time.
